title: IBM Watson Assistant Dialog Conformance & Provenance Catalog
description: Deterministic behavioral specifications and provenance mapping between official IBM rules and test oracles.

entries.description: Nodes in a sibling group are evaluated in sequential order from top to bottom.
entries.expected_behavior: First matching sibling is selected; remaining siblings in the group are skipped unless jumped to.

entries.description: Folder nodes organize sibling groups without creating separate conversational nesting levels.
entries.expected_behavior: Root nodes inside root folders remain root-level nodes for runtime evaluation.

entries.description: Special conditions: 'welcome' matches first turn without input; 'conversation_start' matches first turn regardless of input.
entries.expected_behavior: Condition evaluates true during first turn under documented conditions.

entries.description: anything_else serves as conversational catchall / fallback at the bottom of the dialog.
entries.expected_behavior: Matches when no prior non-fallback root node condition evaluated to true.

entries.description: Shorthand syntax #intent, @entity, @entity:(value), $variable are parsed and evaluated.
entries.expected_behavior: Shorthands resolve against intents list, entities dict/list, and context variables.

entries.description: Partial SpEL evaluator handles common safe subset (.toLowerCase(), .filter(), arithmetic, comparisons); unsupported complex expressions return UNKNOWN safely without throwing runtime crashes.
entries.expected_behavior: A partial evaluation does not imply the official IBM Watson runtime would reject the expression.

entries.description: Dialog-node context values can embed SpEL by using the <? expression ?> evaluation syntax; malformed embedded templates are validated without executing them.
entries.expected_behavior: Context strings may contain one or more expression templates; unclosed delimiters and unambiguous lexical/syntax defects are reported at the nested context field path.

entries.description: Slots gather required context variables in declaration order before completing the parent frame.
entries.expected_behavior: Frame stays active until all mandatory slots are filled or a jump/cancellation is triggered.

entries.description: Digressions allow jumping to root nodes and returning to the interrupted slot or node using a LIFO return stack.
entries.expected_behavior: Return stack pops in LIFO order; abandoned if a digression target triggers an explicit non-returning jump.

entries.description: Jump to 'condition', 'response' (body), or 'user_input' routes execution deterministically to the target node.
entries.expected_behavior: Immediate jumps execute within current turn; user_input jumps set cursor for the following turn.

entries.description: External network webhooks and Actions are not dispatched over HTTP by the local deterministic test runner; effects/results are injected declaratively via scenario fixtures.
entries.expected_behavior: Network-free determinism guarantees zero external side effects.

entries.description: The special false condition can deliberately disable normal branch evaluation while the node remains available as configured content or an alternate jump target.
entries.expected_behavior: Explicit false is classified as deliberate disabled-node evidence rather than an accidental contradiction warning; graph normal-flow reachability remains blocked.

entries.description: A numeric slot that must recognize zero should use a condition that admits zero so zero-specific validation or response handling can execute.
entries.expected_behavior: Bare @sys-number is not blanket-rejected; a warning is emitted only when the slot itself proves that zero must be recognized or when the processed input type contradicts the capture condition.

entries.description: Digression away can be prevented by a forcing catch-all child or an explicit forced transition/skip path.
entries.expected_behavior: The validator reports the documented conflict only for operational source paths; project-local inactive/review status is used as a confidence qualifier rather than promoted to an IBM primitive.
